target: docs/odp/07-alternatives.md (continuum between two values: chestnut colour PATO_0104329 to black PATO_0000317)
reason: A colour between chestnut-brown and black, written as a hyphenated pair of two existing colour values. It is a continuum, not a new colour term.
Green only for part of the year, the opposite of evergreen (PATO_0001733). The plant's green shoots or foliage die back seasonally, which is what deciduous (plant) means.
French 'sans gibbosité(s)' on the standard (banner petal) = not swollen on one side: the negation of FLOPO gibbous.
Members of a set of like parts having the same size: exactly the definition of FLOPO equal.
Close-fitting sheaths lie closely against the stem they surround, which is FLOPO appressed. The other part (the stem) is implicit, as with other appressed statements.
Fruticulose = like a small shrub, a shrubby habit of the whole plant. The existing frutescent habit class covers it; the smallness is not a separate quality.

target: new: quality of the indumentum (comose FLOPO:0991171 + white PATO_0000323 on the hairs)
reason: Two values with different bearers: the anther tip bears a tuft of hairs (comose), and the colour belongs to the hairs, not the anther. A single term would mix the two.

target: docs/odp/07-alternatives.md (conjunction of two values: bent PATO_0000617 and jointed FLOPO:0991154)
reason: Fruiting styles (as in Geum) are both bent like a knee and jointed at the bend: two existing values that both hold, not a new quality.
The single example 'sporangium vertically bisected' could mean how the sporangium splits open or how a section was cut. It is too unclear to map to split (PATO_0001786).
Squamose = covered with scales, the same reading as lepidote in the previous review (PATO_0001804 scaly).
Tomentellate = finely or slightly tomentose: short, dense, matted hairs. At 14 statements in one flora, the existing term is preferred over a diminutive class.
States that the sorus lacks paraphyses (at least centrally). It is an absence of the PO part paraphysis; the 'central bundle' detail stays in the source text.

label: graminoid
definition: A herbaceous quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its having the growth form of a grass: tufted or rhizomatous, with long, narrow, parallel-veined leaves, as in grasses, sedges and rushes. NOTE: Growth-form sibling of the FLOPO frutescent, suffrutescent and arborescent habits; FLOPO_0900037 forbacious is defined as herbaceous other than graminoid.
reason: A standard growth-form category with no term in PATO or FLOPO. FLOPO's forbacious definition already relies on it.
Infundibulate = funnel-shaped, the same as the infundibuliform rule (C218).
'Airy in appearance' is an overall impression of an inflorescence, not a defined quality. Reading it as loose (PATO_0001802) would be a guess.
An inflorescence with its flowers close together is compact, the same as the 'compact' rule (C188, PATO_0001485 condensed).
Bulbate cilia are hairs with a swollen, bulb-like base. PATO bulbous (synonym bulb-shaped, related synonym swollen) is the nearest existing value, although the swelling is at the base only.
A lichen spot-test result (no reaction to KOH) on the lichen medulla and cortex. It is a chemical test outcome on a non-plant, and the pith/cortex bearers are mismappings.
Leaf blades marked with transverse bands of lighter and darker colour (as in Sansevieria). PATO banded is defined as transverse stripes of one hue crossing another.
Beadlike = constricted at intervals like a string of beads, which is FLOPO moniliform; 'not beadlike' is its negation.

target: docs/odp/07-alternatives.md (conjunction of two values: papillose FLOPO:0991059 and swollen) with part of the bearer (proximal part of style)
reason: Two values on one region of the style: papillose and swollen, located proximally. This is a compound plus a part of the bearer, not a single quality.
These are clusters of stone cells in the fruit flesh, and PO has no class for them. Their absence cannot be stated as entity absence yet, and the 'whole plant' bearer is a parsing error.

label: hemielliptic
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having the outline of half an ellipse divided along its long axis, with one side straight and the other evenly curved. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0002232 semicircular; PATO:0000947 elliptic is the whole ellipse.
reason: A defined outline shape of fern pinna lobes and segments. Its nearest PATO sibling, semicircular, covers only the half-circle.

label: hemitelioid
definition: A shape quality inhering in an indusium by virtue of its being a small scale or partial cup attached on the costal side of the sorus, which it only partly encloses. NOTE: One of the indusium types of tree ferns (Cyatheaceae), with cyatheoid, meniscoid and sphaeropteroid; botany-specific.
reason: A defined type of indusium in tree ferns (Cyatheaceae) with no term. It is used in only one flora, so it should go after the more widely used terms.
Veins that fork into two repeatedly. This follows the dichotomous rule (C199) to PATO bifurcated; the repetition does not need its own term.

target: docs/odp/07-alternatives.md (continuum between two values: trigonous FLOPO:0991120 to tetrahedral)
reason: A hyphenated pair of two shape values for the fruit (between three-angled and tetrahedral), like 'oblong-ovate'. It is not one quality.
Not a standard term in botanical glossaries. It is used on very different parts (corolla apex, disc gland, anther, stigma, plica), so its meaning cannot be fixed.
French 'plurinerves', '3 à plurinerves' = several- to many-nerved: a count of veins (open-ended, 3 to many), like '5-nerved'.
French 'subéperonnées à la base' = wing petals with a small, spur-like projection at the base. Record petal spur as present and treat 'sub-' as approximate (docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md).
Rhizome scales of one colour throughout, as opposed to bicolorous or clathrate scales, which is FLOPO concolorous.
